drhp.business: Kotak Mahindra Bank provides a comprehensive suite of financial solutions across customer segments and geographies in India, anchored by four interconnected engines: Banking & Lending, Capital Markets, Asset Management, and Protection. The Group serves over 5.2 crore customers through a physical network of 5,581 locations and digital platforms, targeting HNIs, SMEs, Core India retail, and institutional clients. All subsidiaries are 100% beneficially owned by the Bank, enabling integrated product manufacturing and distribution while retaining full profitability within the Group.

risks.note: Credit risk is the most significant risk for the Group, arising from potential failure of borrowers or counterparties to meet obligations. Deterioration in repayment capacity, sector stress, or macroeconomic shocks could impair asset quality and profitability.
risks.risk: Credit Risk â Asset Quality Deterioration

risks.note: RBI reduced the policy repo rate by 100 basis points during the year, leading to NIM compression across the banking sector. Sustained low-rate environment or competitive pricing pressure could further compress margins.

Regulatory constraints that had restricted certain digital onboarding and credit card business activities were lifted only in February 2025. Future regulatory actions or non-compliance could again restrict business capacity or impose penalties.

Increasing reliance on digital channels and data-driven operations heightens exposure to cyber threats, data breaches, and service disruptions, which can lead to regulatory penalties, reputational damage, and loss of customer trust.
risks.risk: Data Security and Privacy / Cyber Risk

risks.note: Inadequate integration of climate and ESG risks in lending and investment decisions may affect credit quality and portfolio resilience. The Bank strengthened its Environmental and Social risk framework during the year, embedding it into credit decisions.

Credit risk concentration is actively managed to prevent excessive exposure to individual borrowers, groups, sectors, or geographies. Breach of concentration limits could amplify losses in a downturn.

The Group maintains prudent buffers above regulatory minima, but adverse macroeconomic scenarios or unexpected losses could strain capital adequacy, requiring capital conservation or constraining growth.
